transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-09
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Jared Collins (NovaFind Head of Search), Maya Singh (NovaFind ML), Liam O'Neill (NovaFind CTO)
---
Summary (auto): quick hosted API demo focused on embeddings + reranking for search relevance; showed Redwood Console, API samples, and an initial batch of example rerank outputs; discussed privacy/SOC2 and pilot logistics.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, um appreciate you taking the time. I'm Samir from Redwood, with me is Elena, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Jared: Good thanks, busy week but excited to see this.
[00:09] Maya: Hi all, thanks, we sent over a sample of queries earlier.
[00:12] Elena: Great, we pulled a small slice and prepared a few quick runs to show relevance differences, and we'll walk through API calls and console too.
[00:20] Liam: Quick heads up, our main goals are improve MAP@10 by at least 8%, keep P95 latency under 200ms for rerank calls, and make sure we don't leak PII - so SOC2 + KMS is needed.
[00:32] Samir: Sounds good, that matches what we saw on the intake form. We'll show hosted flow first, talk about Dedicated if we hit scale or have strict network reqs.
[00:40] Elena: Ok jumping in, first slide, hosted embeddings endpoint. The call is a simple POST embeddings with text inputs, we support various vector dims and models, and you can configure batching and caching. Example curl: curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" -d '{"input": ["query text"]}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'
[01:05] Maya: Are embeddings returned deterministically? We need stable vectors across re-indexes.
[01:09] Elena: Good question — yes, with a pinned model version we ensure deterministic embeddings; note small float-level variance can occur between quantized builds but pinned versions avoid surprises.
[01:22] Jared: How do you handle schema for multi-field docs? We have product title, description, FAQ, and faceted metadata.
[01:28] Elena: Typically we embed title+description for semantic relevance and keep faceted metadata in search index for filters; we showed an example of per-field weighting in the reranker.
[01:35] Samir: We'll show the rerank endpoint next — that's where you send the original candidate list (IDs + scores) plus the query embedding and the model returns reranked scores.
[01:45] Elena: Quick demo — I have our NovaFind sample dataset preloaded; first I'm calling the hosted embeddings endpoint for the query "best wireless headphones for travel".
[01:52] [01:56] Elena: (typing) curl... now returning embedding, size 768, latency ~40ms for this request from west-us region.
[02:05] Maya: 40ms is pretty good. What's tokenization overhead like?
[02:09] Elena: For short queries it's minimal, total time here dominated by model infer plus networking; for batch of queries we recommend our batch endpoint to amortize per-request overhead.
[02:20] Samir: Ok now rerank call — I'm sending top-50 candidates from your current search index, with their original BM25 scores, then our reranker takes those + the query embedding.
[02:30] [02:33] Elena: (executing) request posted, we're using the small rerank model variant for lower cost. Response back in ~110ms, reranked list shows two items moving up that look semantically closer.
[02:42] Jared: Can you show the before/after relevance metrics?
[02:45] Elena: Sure, here's a small table — baseline MAP@10 was 0.42, after rerank MAP@10 is 0.51 on the 1k sample, so roughly +9%. Caveats: this is a smaller sample and we tuned thresholds.
[02:58] Liam: That delta aligns with what we want. What's cost per query at that latency?
[03:05] Samir: For the small rerank model on hosted it's roughly $0.002 per rerank call at this scale; embeddings are about $0.0005 per vector. We'll include detailed pricing in the follow-up.
[03:18] Maya: How do we handle caching? We have many repeated queries from internal users.
[03:22] Elena: Redwood provides prefix and KV caching at the edge for hosted requests; you can set TTLs per route in the Console. That reduced our token costs in other customers by 30-40% on repeat traffic.
[03:34] Jared: Security — we need SOC2, SSO, and our own KMS for keys.
[03:39] Samir: Redwood is SOC2 Type II, and hosted customers can bring their own KMS via cloud KMS integrations for enterprise plans; SSO / SAML and RBAC are supported. We'll attach the security pack.
[03:50] Liam: Do you retain raw queries or do you offer no-retention options?
[03:55] Elena: We offer data retention controls: for hosted pilots we can enable minimal retention and audit logs; for strict no-retention we recommend Private deployment or a Dedicated flow with local logging.
[04:06] Maya: For the pilot we can accept hosted with minimal retention if we can keep PII out and have proper logging.
[04:11] Samir: Great. Next I'll show the Redwood Console — quick glance at routes, per-route latency and cost, token breakdown, and the rerank route dashboard.
[04:20] [04:25] Elena: Console — here's the rerank route, the trace shows a 110ms tail, 70ms model time, 40ms network. We can set SLOs and alerts. Also you can pin model versions per route so experiments are reproducible.
[04:40] Jared: For A/B testing, can we do canary rollouts between rerank models?
[04:43] Elena: Yes, Console supports canary, A/B, and automatic fallback policies if latency spikes; we can route 10% to a new reranker and measure MAP/CTR.
[04:52] Maya: How do we integrate with our existing ranking stack? We're using Elastic for retrieval and then a downstream ranker.
[04:57] Elena: The integration pattern is: retrieve candidates from Elastic, call Redwood embeddings and rerank endpoints, and write back or just return reranked IDs to the serving layer. We have SDK snippets for Python/Go and a sample microservice template.
[05:10] Liam: If we scale to 2k QPS during peak, what's the path?
[05:14] Samir: For that scale we'd discuss Redwood Dedicated or autoscaling reserved capacity; hosted can handle bursts but Dedicated offers predictable throughput, GPU pools, and private networking. We'll bring in a Dedicated pricing sheet if you want to explore.
[05:25] Jared: Are there any gotchas with vector dims and our existing similarity search? We store 512-d vectors in Milvus today.
[05:31] Elena: You can choose model dims; we can return 512 or 768 depending on model. If you want to keep Milvus, we recommend embedding all docs with the same dim; otherwise Redwood can host embeddings and do end-to-end similarity + rerank.
[05:45] Maya: Can Redwood host the index or do we need to maintain Milvus?
[05:49] Samir: We integrate with hosted vector stores or you can keep yours. Many customers use Redwood only for inference and keep their vector store; others move to our managed path for simplicity.
[05:59] Jared: Ok real quick can we see an example of API error handling and retries?
[06:03] Elena: Sure — standard 5xx backoff, idempotency keys for long-running jobs; for streaming generation we have chunked responses but rerank/embeddings are synchronous.
[06:14] [06:20] Elena: I'm running one more rerank variant — larger reranker model for higher quality. This one is ~220ms but MAP@10 increases to 0.55 on the sample.
[06:31] Maya: So tradeoff is cost + latency versus quality, yep expected.
[06:35] Samir: Exactly. For the pilot we usually start with small rerank for cost-effectiveness, then test a medium model for quality uplift and run a small canary.
[06:45] Jared: About the benchmark — can you run it on our 1k queries? We can provide the subset with labels.
[06:50] Elena: Yes that's the plan — Elena will run it and share the result and the latency/cost spreadsheet.
[06:56] Liam: SLA question — do you offer uptime SLA for hosted?
[06:59] Samir: Hosted has a commercial SLA on enterprise tier; Dedicated has stronger contractual uptime and latency guarantees. We'll include SLA options in the follow-up.
[07:10] Jared: Any compliance red flags for EU data residency? We have EU customers and need data not to leave EU.
[07:16] Samir: We operate regional hosted endpoints; for strict residency you can use Private deployments or our EU regions; we'll include region-specific details in the security pack.
[07:25] Maya: One more technical — do you store KV cache in Redis or in-process? How does cache warmup work?
[07:30] Elena: We have a managed KV cache layer; for Dedicated/Private you can bring your own Redis/managed cache. Warmup is done by pre-populating frequent prefixes or running a synthetic traffic profile.
[07:42] Jared: Cool. Any blockers to starting the pilot?
[07:45] Liam: None from infra, but legal needs the SOW and security docs.
[07:49] Samir: We'll send SOW + security pack.
[07:52] Elena: I'll start the benchmark once we receive the sample.
[07:55] Jared: Sounds good.
[07:57] Samir: Quick recap — Samir to send pricing and SOW by 11/11, Elena to run 1k-query benchmark by 11/13, NovaFind to share labeled subset by 11/12. We'll reconvene after benchmark results to decide next steps and whether to try a medium reranker.
[08:15] Maya: Thanks everyone, this was useful.
[08:18] Liam: Thanks, appreciate it.
[08:20] Samir: Thanks, talk soon.
---
